curriculumMapping.practical: Determination of strength of a given solution of sodium hydroxide by titrating it against standard oxalic acid solution.
learningObjectives: Prepare and use a standard solution of oxalic acid
Perform a titration using a pipette, burette and conical flask
Select phenolphthalein for a weak-acid/strong-base endpoint
Apply N₁V₁ = N₂V₂ and calculate strength in g/L
curriculumMapping.sourceReference: CBSE Chemistry (043) Classes XI-XII Curriculum 2026-27, PRACTICAL SYLLABUS, E. Quantitative Estimation

title: Volumetric analysis: strength of NaOH by titration with oxalic acid
objective: Prepare a standard oxalic acid solution.
Determine the strength of sodium hydroxide by titration.
Express the result in normality, molarity and grams per litre.

theory.statement: At equivalence, acid and base react in chemically equivalent amounts.
theory.derivationNote: Oxalic acid dihydrate, H₂C₂O₄·2H₂O, is a primary standard. The equivalence pH is slightly basic because oxalate hydrolysis occurs.

procedure.text: Dissolve the accurately weighed oxalic acid dihydrate in distilled water and make up to volume.
Rinse and fill the burette with standard oxalic acid; remove air bubbles.
Pipette the measured NaOH into the conical flask and add phenolphthalein.
Run acid rapidly at first, then dropwise near the first permanent loss of pink colour.
Repeat until concordant titres are obtained and calculate using N₁V₁ = N₂V₂.

safety: Sodium hydroxide is corrosive; wear eye protection.
Never pipette by mouth; use a pipette filler.
Oxalic acid is harmful if swallowed.
Phenolphthalein in ethanol is flammable; keep away from flames.

duringLab.question: Use phenolphthalein for this weak-acid/strong-base titration.

assumptions: NaOH is treated as fully dissociated
scientificValidation.validRange: Burette 0–50 mL; pipette 5–25 mL; concentration 0.02–0.5 N
scientificValidation.unitSystem: Volumes in mL; normality in eq/L; strength in g/L
edgeCases: At equivalence pH is basic, not exactly 7
expectedBehaviour: pH decreases as acid is delivered
Concordant titres give a stable mean
